items.text: Occupational therapy suits people who want to help others regain the daily activities that matter to them, such as dressing, writing, working or playing, and it is a good career only if you can handle patient-facing clinical work, slow progress and the registration rules that apply.
It is a regulated allied health career built on helping people function in daily life.
Course recognition, registration and scope of practice differ by state and council.
